transcript.text:
I can help with that. 'Stopped working' on a hoover usually comes down to one of three things: it's not getting power, a safety cut-out has triggered (often due to overheating or blockage), or there's an internal fault. To narrow this down quickly:
1. Is your vacuum corded or cordless?
2. If corded: check the plug is tight in the socket and that no other appliances on that circuit have lost power (which would suggest a tripped breaker). Also, check the fuse inside the plug if you're comfortable doing so.
3. If cordless: ensure it's charged for at least 30 minutes before trying again. Please let me know which type it is and what you find with the power source.
its corded. the red one, Henry. the socket works, my lamp works in it. nothing happens when i switch it on

Since the socket is live but Henry does nothing when switched on, the most likely cause is a blown fuse in the plug, followed by a faulty on/off switch or a damaged cable. Please unplug the vacuum first for safety.
1. Check the plug: open it and see if the 13A fuse has blown (the thin metal wire inside will be broken). If you have a spare 13A fuse, try swapping it in.
2. Inspect the cable: look along its entire length for any cuts, crush marks or damage, especially near where it enters the plug and the vacuum body.
3. Check the switch: with the plug out, wiggle the on/off switch slightly while looking at the plug pins; if you see a spark or flicker when moving the switch, the switch contacts are likely faulty. Let me know what you find with the fuse and cable.

I haven't got a screwdriver or a spare fuse so can't open the plug. There's black tape round the wire near the plug, my son did it ages ago, and it's a bit bent there. Once it came on for a second when I moved the wire but I'm not doing that again, it frightened me.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Stop using it now. If you can do it safely, switch it off at the socket or at the consumer unit (fuse box). A shock usually means an earth or insulation fault, so don't use it again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has found and fixed it. Because the wire is bent and taped, and it sparked when you moved it, this is a serious electric shock hazard. Do not use the vacuum again. You cannot safely fix a damaged mains cable or internal wiring without special tools and skills. Please take it to a qualified appliance engineer or a local repair shop who can check the plug or cable assembly properly. If you are unsure where to go, a local electrical goods store may be able to fit a new plug on a good-quality cable if the vacuum body itself is sound.

candidates: Power supply issue (unplugged, tripped fuse, dead battery) (high)
plan: The fault they reported is: "stopped working". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
